chunks: There is no compulsion in matter of faith. Distinct is the way of guidance now from error. He who turns away from the forces of evil and believes in God, will surely hold fast to a handle that is strong and unbreakable, for God hears all and knows everything.

key_terms.الطَّاغُوت: False deities or forces of evil
key_terms.الْعُرْوَةُ الْوُثْقَى: The unbreakable handle (metaphor for firm connection to God)

ai.seo_question: What does 'no compulsion in religion' mean in Shia theology?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse is often interpreted as establishing the intrinsic validity of faith, where 'clear distinction' (Tabayyuna) refers to the clarity of truth through the Imams and Prophets, rendering external coercion unnecessary. The 'unbreakable handle' (Urwah al-Wuthqa) is frequently identified by scholars like Al-Tabarsi and Al-Kulayni as the Ahl al-Bayt, emphasizing that true adherence to God is inextricably linked to accepting their spiritual authority.
